resolutions.title: Sarah Holman and Mary White: incompatible dates
resolutions.baseline_conflict: Sarah Holman’s stored birth date equals her marriage date. Mary White’s stored 1728 birth would make her about two at the recorded 1730 marriage; daughters born after her stored 1731 death also require review.
resolutions.competing_claims: These are incompatible repository fields, not grounds to invent replacement dates. Essex notes assign Susannah, Mary and Jane to Sarah, unlike portions of the repository.
resolutions.conclusion: February 7, 1733/34 is a documented marriage date, not an established birth date for Sarah Holman. Suppress the unsupported exact birth in the effective profile; retain its original value here. Mary White’s dates and the daughters’ maternity remain unresolved.
resolutions.reasoning: The 1904 marriage transcription explicitly places both James marriages under marriages. The 1905 Essex note assigns Susannah, Mary and Jane to Sarah. These derivative accounts may use the same records; they do not supply Sarah’s birth or prove Mary’s vital dates. Do not substitute the 1706 Sarah Holman found in user trees without identity proof.
resolutions.identity_reasoning: Groom James, bride Sarah, place and day match the stored marriage. James Jr. has a stored 1724 birth and is a separate profile; no reassignment of the marriages or children is made.

changes.reason: Stored date matches the documented marriage; no birth evidence located.

resolutions.title: A Thomas Beverage deed cited after his death

resolutions.competing_claims: Could be recording date, estate action or another Thomas. Original execution and acknowledgment clauses must be checked; no death-date correction is justified.
resolutions.conclusion: No death-date or property correction is justified. The 1837 date remains an unresolved deed citation; it has not been shown to be execution, recording or estate action.
resolutions.reasoning: The Woodruff note provides an exact DGS/page/image target but only a generic FamilySearch link. Direct film/catalog retrieval was inaccessible. Seaview transcription lists Capt. Thomas’s death October 4, 1834 and spouse Mercy, supporting the need to inspect the deed rather than assume a later death.
resolutions.identity_reasoning: The deed parties alone do not distinguish Capt. Thomas from another Thomas or a posthumous transaction.

resolutions.title: Two Sarahs linked to Benjamin Kent

fields.notes: Daughter of James Beveridge Jr.; married Benjamin Kent.
Daughter of Thomas and Mercy; married Benjamin Kent, creating double in‑law tie.
Shipbuilder and brother to Mercy Kent; married Sarah 'Sally' Beverage.

resolutions.baseline_conflict: The Kent cemetery transcription calls Sarah Beverage Kent, deceased November 23, 1821 aged 63 years 5 months, a sister of Capt. Thomas. She must not be merged with his daughter Sarah Sally, born 1785.
resolutions.competing_claims: Repository links both women to Benjamin Kent 1755. A duplicated transcription line says s.o., the fuller line says sis.o.; use original stone and marriages to distinguish them.
resolutions.conclusion: The older Sarah Kent and Thomas’s daughter Sarah Sally must remain separate. The older Sarah is the more plausible wife in the Kent family evidence, but the spouse links cannot yet be conclusively reassigned.
resolutions.reasoning: Kent cemetery gives Sarah’s age as 63 years 5 months at her 1821 death, consistent with about 1758, and its fuller duplicate line says sister of Capt. Thomas. The Woodruff junior biography cites that same cemetery entry, so it is dependent rather than independent proof. A separate Seaview Sarah died in 1844 at 59 years 8 months.
resolutions.identity_reasoning: The two deaths, ages, and sister-versus-daughter generations distinguish the women; Benjamin junior’s 1798 birth also makes Sarah born 1785 an implausible mother. Neither age arithmetic nor later narrative proves the marriage.
resolutions.remaining_question: Obtain Benjamin senior’s marriage, the original Kent stone and the Vinalhaven Kent family register. Verify senior’s own birth year, too; a user-tree lead gives 1760 rather than stored 1755.
resolutions.retrieval_request: NHHS: please provide photographs or original transcription worksheets for Sarah (Beverage) Kent, died November 23, 1821 aged 63y 5m, and Sarah Beverage, Seaview, died November 1844 aged 59y 8m. Please clarify s.o. versus sis.o. in the Kent PDF. Vinalhaven clerk: please locate Benjamin and Sarah Kent’s marriage/family entries, including Benjamin junior in DGS 7596929 p. 389, image 215/837.

resolutions.competing_claims: Years and island career suggest the same person, but original birth and Harvard records are needed. Preserve both spellings and locations.
resolutions.conclusion: A contemporary Harvard newspaper supports the Eliot P. Beveridge spelling and education connection. Massachusetts birthplace remains plausible but unproved; keep the existing profile name and birthplace while exposing the alternative in research and search.
resolutions.reasoning: The Crimson identifies Eliot P. Beveridge, Harvard A.B. 1930 and A.M. 1931, in 1934; NHHS independently describes Eliot’s Harvard education, island business and 1908–1982 lifespan. Neither the newspaper’s residence nor NHHS narrative substitutes for a birth entry. The online newspaper spells the place Derchester; preserve the transcription caveat.
resolutions.identity_reasoning: Name, middle initial, educational chronology and NHHS life dates support association. Exact birth and parentage still require a certificate or Harvard biographical file. Search expansion is not an identity merge.

resolutions.title: Two Amelia profiles requiring identity review
resolutions.baseline_conflict: Two repository IDs appear to describe the same wife of Benjamin Crabtree and daughter of Norwood and Hannah; birth dates differ January 31 versus January 1, 1833.
resolutions.competing_claims: Duplicate suspected from shared relations, not merged. January 1 is already treated as year-only by the repository precision system.
resolutions.conclusion: The duplicate hypothesis is strong, but both IDs remain available pending an original record linking Amelia’s parentage and marriage. January 1 is a year placeholder and is not a second exact birth claim.
resolutions.reasoning: Both profiles share two parents, the same spouse, all nine children, six siblings, and 1833–1908 dates; this is much more than a name match. However both cite a generic Find A Grave memorial, so they are not independent evidence. Seaview names Amelia as Benjamin C.’s wife but also contains a birth-column defect; no exact date is adopted from it.
resolutions.identity_reasoning: The full shared family cluster strongly suggests one intended person. Retaining both IDs prevents an unreviewed identity consolidation; related-profile links make the suspected duplicate explicit.
resolutions.remaining_question: Obtain Amelia’s 1908 death certificate or marriage record naming parents Norwood and Hannah Grant. If confirmed, consolidate with a canonical ID and compatibility alias in a later reviewed change.
resolutions.retrieval_request: North Haven clerk / Maine State Archives: please locate Amelia Beverage, widow of Benjamin Crabtree Beverage, died in 1908 (Seaview transcription suggests February 16), born about 1833, reportedly daughter of Norwood Beverage and Hannah Grant. Please provide original death and marriage records with parents and birth information. The exact January 31 birth remains unverified.
